claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for release because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and a reversible monitored 3% rollout makes launch supportable despite a known below-target health-plan benefits support limitation.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the affected use case is excluded from launch, the policy concern is materially reduced.
If admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance specifically covers the exposed segment, the policy predicate could be satisfied.
If admissible evidence shows explicit launch-time model-card disclosure is finalized and certification policy permits launch with disclosed unresolved limitations, the verdict could improve.
Without one of those support links, certification remains under-supported.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual launch-bound model card or disclosure artifact showing the health-plan benefits support limitation is explicitly disclosed.
Provide approval or publication evidence that the required disclosure will accompany the certified release.
Provide any reviewed risk acceptance, if one exists, that specifically addresses the exposed health-plan benefits support segment.
Provide the governing certification criterion showing whether disclosure plus monitoring is sufficient for certification despite an unresolved below-target named use case.
specific_concerns: The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The actor summary states the below-target health-plan benefits support segment remains in the initial rollout cohort.
The unsigned risk acceptance draft cannot satisfy the policy predicate because it is not approved and does not address the exposed segment.
Certification is described as defensible only if there is explicit model-card disclosure, but no admissible evidence here shows that disclosure is finalized, approved, or bound to launch.
unsupported_claims: The recommended action 'certify_model' is not fully supported unless explicit launch-time model-card disclosure is itself evidenced.
Any implication that rollback, dashboards, monitoring, or a 3% rollout alone resolve the material weakness is unsupported under the stated policy.
Any implication that risk acceptance covers the exposed segment is unsupported.
